paragraphs.text: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD) is an inherited kidney disease. It usually begins between the third and seventh decades and is mainly characterized by fluid-filled cysts forming in the kidneys. Disease caused by PKD2 mutations follows a course very similar to that of PKD1 disease. However, patients with PKD2 mutations have a milder course: on average, onset is 10 to 20 years later and they are less likely to reach end-stage renal failure (Deltas, 2001). Mutations in PKD2 are expected to account for approximately 15% of ADPKD cases (Torra et al., 1999).

paragraphs.text: Bachner et al. (1990) described a large 3-generation family with ADPKD. Ultrasound screening of 60 family members found 20 individuals, aged 10 to 80 years, with one or several cysts in only one kidney, and 7 individuals with cysts in both kidneys. The authors concluded that this family had a form of ADPKD with reduced penetrance and no linkage to the PKD1 locus. They also considered other explanations, including 2 distinct hereditary diseases in the family, or a new mutation in one branch of the family together with a high frequency of isolated renal cysts.

paragraphs.text: Ravine et al. (1992) compared 18 families (285 affected members) with mutations at the PKD1 locus with 5 families (49 affected individuals) in which involvement of PKD1 could be dismissed. Compared with PKD1 patients, non-PKD1 patients: - lived longer (median survival 71.5 vs 56.0 years); - had a lower risk of progressing to renal failure (odds ratio 0.35); - were less likely to have hypertension (adjusted odds ratio 0.29); - were diagnosed at an older age (median 69.1 vs 44.8 years); - had fewer renal cysts at diagnosis. No non-PKD1 family was identified through clinics treating patients with renal impairment. The authors concluded that non-PKD1 ADPKD has a much milder phenotype and that its prevalence is probably underestimated.

paragraphs.text: In a multicenter European survey, Hateboer et al. (1999) compared 333 people with PKD1 (31 families), 291 people with PKD2 (31 families) and 398 geographically matched controls. Median age at death or onset of ESRD was 53.0 years with PKD1, 69.1 years with PKD2, and 78.0 years in controls. Women with PKD2 had a significantly longer median survival than men (71.0 vs 67.3 years), whereas no sex effect was seen in PKD1. Patients with PKD2 presented with kidney failure later than those with PKD1 (median age 74.0 vs 54.3 years). They were also less likely to have hypertension, a history of urinary tract infection, or hematuria. The authors concluded that although PKD2 is clinically milder than PKD1, it shortens overall life expectancy and cannot be regarded as benign.
